Optimization strategy based on robust model predictive control for 
RES-CCHP system under multiple uncertainties 
Xing Dong , Chenghui Zhang
*
, Bo Sun 
School of Control Science and Engineering, Shandong University, Jingshi Road 17923, Jinan 250061, China   
HIGHLIGHTS 
• An integrated framework is constructed to coordinate prediction and optimization. 
• An optimization strategy based on robust model predictive control is proposed. 
• A min – max rolling optimization model of the RES-CCHP system is presented. 
• Source-load probability distribution is modeled by the Gaussian process regression.  
ARTICLE INFO  
Keywords: 
RES-CCHP system 
Multiple uncertainties 
Uncertain rolling optimization framework 
Robust model predictive control 
ABSTRACT  
The economic operation of renewable energy sources (RES) integrated with a combined cooling, heating, and 
power system significantly improves energy utilization and reduces environmental crises. However, multiple 
uncertainties in RES generation and load consumption predictions cause an imbalance between supply and 
demand, negatively impacting system efficiency and economics. To address this limitation, an integrated un -
certainty rolling optimization framework for combining the probability distribution of prediction and uncer -
tainty optimization is established. Under this framework, an optimization strategy based on a robust model 
predictive control is proposed for handling the multiple uncertainties of source-load. Here, the probability dis -
tributions of RES generation and load consumption predictions are determined using the Gaussian process 
regression method, and a minimum – maximum rolling optimization model is developed. Under the uncertain 
scenarios of RES generation and load consumption, the optimization model is converted into a tractable form to 
obtain a robust schedule that minimizes operating costs. The over-conservatism of robust optimization can be 
mitigated by adjusting the uncertainty budget. Many case studies are further conducted to confirm the effec -
tiveness of the proposed method. Results show that the operating costs decreased by 11.5% compared with the 
traditional model predictive control strategies in an uncertain scenario.   
1. Introduction 
The supply and consumption of energy are the basis of rapid eco -
nomic development [1] . However, the depletion of energy sources and 
climate issues have attracted considerable attention globally. For sus -
tainable economic development, it is essential to increase the penetra -
tion of renewable energy sources (RES) [2] . Incorporating RES into 
combined cooling, heating, and power (RES-CCHP) systems can improve 
primary energy utilization by combining many energy sources [3] . As 
the RES-CCHP system has a high energy efficiency, it has been exten -
sively used to provide electricity, heating, and cooling for campuses [4] 
and commercial buildings [5] . However, RES generation and load 
consumption fluctuate considerably (source-load uncertainties), seri -
ously affecting the operation performance of RES-CCHP systems [6] . The 
problem usually needs to be solved using advanced operation optimi -
zation methods [7] . The implementation of operation optimization 
primarily includes two parts: (1) prediction of RES generation and loads 
consumption (source-load prediction) and (2) modeling of the optimi -
zation strategy (OS). The literature review is discussed separately for 
these two parts in the subsequent paragraphs. 
First, source-load prediction is the input to the OS, and accurate 
prediction is conducive to improving the optimization effect. Currently, 
prediction methods (PMs) have been increasingly studied. In Ref. [8] , 
the general trend of wind energy is predicted using artificial intelligence 
technology and data fusion algorithm through various neural networks.

In Ref. [9] , a deep learning model with a dynamic scene cross-generation 
algorithm of photovoltaic power generation was established to improve 
prediction accuracy. Concerning the load forecast, to improve the sta -
bility of the forecasting model, a short-term power-load-forecasting 
method, including error correction based on dynamic mode decompo -
sition, has been proposed [10] . In Ref. [11] , a novel dense average 
connection structure was proposed to realize a short-term load-fore -
casting, and an integrated method was applied to reduce the forecast 
deviation. For predicting cooling, heating, and power load in CCHP 
systems, a forecasting model based on an autoregressive moving average 
with exogenous inputs has been proposed [12] . The abovementioned 
forecasting methods only determine the forecast value, whereas the 
forecasting model based on Gaussian process regression (GPR) can 
predict the source-load probability distribution. A multitask GPR model 
[13] and a hybrid model that combines long short-term memory with 
GPR [14] have been proposed to predict renewable energy generation. 
To solve the problem of unreasonable training set selection, a short-term 
load-forecasting model based on the combination of density value 
clustering and GPR has been established [15] . 
Second, OSs are important for improving system operations. Initially, 
scholars mainly studied the day-ahead OSs to develop efficient and 
economical source-load matching plans. In Ref. [16] , an OS considering 
multiple objectives was established, and a new electrical load-tracking 
strategy was proposed to improve energy utilization as per the energy 
requirements of buildings. In Ref. [17] , to promote the low-carbon 
operation of a CCHP system, a bilevel carbon pricing OS was devel -
oped, and a bisection method was proposed to obtain effective 
incentives. In Ref. [18] , a trilayer OS of multi-time – space scale was 
established to guarantee the energy supply and load demand balance. In 
Ref. [19] , to improve the system ’ s economy, a dynamic model of a CCHP 
system pipe network was proposed, and a day-ahead OS considering 
energy storage units was proposed. In Ref. [20] , an OS considering 
multi-objective and nonlinear constraints was developed, and a gray 
wolf solution algorithm was proposed, significantly improving the en -
ergy efficiency. However, the intermittent nature of RES and the 
randomness of the customer loads negatively affect the operation of the 
RES-CCHP system [21] . To address this limitation, in Ref. [22] , a day- 
ahead OS, including load and RES uncertainty, was established, and 
benefiting from the advantages of digital twins, the operating costs of 
the CCHP system were reduced. To guarantee the stable operation of a 
CCHP system with uncertainty in the RES power generation, an adaptive 
robust OS has been established [23] . In Ref. [24] , a multiple thermal 
inertia model of a CCHP system was studied, and a robust OS containing 
the thermal inertia uncertainty was proposed, which increased the 
thermal network ’ s heat storage capacity. In Ref. [25] , a CCHP model, 
including an energy recovery system, was developed, and a two-stage 
robust OS considering the RES uncertainty and water inrush was 
adopted to fully improve the energy recovery, economic benefits, and 
operational robustness. In Ref. [26] , robustness was introduced into a 
genetic algorithm, and a multi-objective robust OS of the CCHP system 
was established to evaluate the system ’ s environmental impact. In 
Ref. [27] , to ensure the stable operation of a CCHP microgrid system in 
case of a small number of source-load samples, an adaptive kernel 
density estimator was used to predict the source-load probability

distribution, and a day-ahead uncertainty OS based on probabilistic 
chance constraints was proposed. The foregoing day-ahead OSs have 
made significant contributions to the operation of CCHP systems. 
However, with the increasing uncertainty of source and load, these day- 
ahead OSs cannot adjust the schedules on an intraday basis in response 
to rapid changes in RES and customer loads, which affects the intraday ’ s 
economical and efficient operation of the system. 
To address the defects of the day-ahead OSs, the rolling optimization 
technology based on the model predictive control (MPC) method has 
been extensively studied [28] . In the MPC-based optimization, the sys -
tem ’ s future state can be obtained using a predictive model, and a rolling 
OS determines the output sequence in a limited time horizon. Moreover, 
feedback adjustments can be implemented as per the current status at 
each optimization interval. For the economic dispatch of a CCHP 
microgrids system, in Ref. [29] , an OS combining dynamic time interval 
and MPC was proposed to optimize the system ’ s operating costs. In 
Ref. [30] , an MPC model based on affine technology was proposed, 
which provided a cost-effective solution. In Ref. [31] , an OS combining a 
day-ahead distributionally robust chance-constrained optimization 
model with an MPC-based rolling optimization model was established to 
trade off economics and operational risks. To realize the real-time 
operation of a CCHP system, an OS combining random day-ahead 
optimization and real-time MPC was proposed in [32] . In Ref. [33] , a 
two-stage coordinated control method was proposed, and in the 
economic-dispatching stage, MPC was used to schedule the system ’ s 
operation. In Ref. [34] , an MPC framework was applied in a scheduling 
method for a CCHP system, including rolling and feedback correction 
parts and it can better achieve source-load matching. The above MPC- 
based OSs can adapt to the rapid changes in the source-load and 
resolve the impact of the day-ahead prediction error on the system 
operation. However, the intraday prediction error caused by source-load 
uncertainty has not been considered in the above MPC-based OS 
modeling, which is unconducive to enhancing the abilities of the sys -
tem ’ s intraday operations in resisting multiple uncertain disturbances. 
Due to the existence of intraday prediction errors, existing MPC- 
based OSs cannot be directly deployed. In addition, dealing with 
intraday prediction errors requires considering time scale differences 
between multiple energy forms, which also increases the complexity of 
the OS. Therefore, to improve the robust and economic performance of 
the intraday operations of the RES-CCHP system under the multiple 
uncertainties of RES generation and load consumption, this study pro -
poses an OS based on robust MPC (RMPC) and considers the uncertainty 
characteristics of source-load in the optimization modeling. The primary 
contributions of this study are summarized as follows:  
(1) An integrated uncertainty rolling optimization framework (ROF) 
that includes the probability distribution of prediction and un -
certainty rolling optimization is established. Specifically, under 
the framework, forecasting and optimization are implemented on 
a rolling time horizon, and the probability distribution of pre -
diction uses different time scales and can be corrected as per the 
system ’ s current state.  
(2) Based on the uncertainty ROF, an RMPC-based OS involving GPR- 
based source-load prediction and minimum – maximum (min -
– max) rolling optimization is proposed. The proposed strategy 
applies the RMPC theory to the optimal operation of the RES- 
CCHP system, and the uncertainty budget parameters are intro -
duced to adjust the robust optimization conservativeness.  
(3) In a source-load uncertainty scenario, the min – max optimization 
model is converted into a tractable form for solving. The case 
study confirms the advantages of the proposed OS by comparing 
it with traditional MPC-based and day-ahead robust OSs. 
The rest of this study is organized as follows: Section 2 describes the 
RES-CCHP system structure and the energy flows. Section 3 introduces 
the integrated uncertainty ROF and the RMPC-based OS. Section 4 in -
troduces the detailed solution process of the min – max rolling optimi -
zation model. Section 5 presents the case study results, and the last 
section concludes the study. 
2. System structure and energy flow analysis 
2.1. RES-CCHP system structure 
Compared with the traditional single energy flow system, the RES- 
CCHP system primarily comprises three energy flows: electrical,

cooling, and heat energy flow. The cascade utilization and comple -
mentary coupling of energy can be realized by coordinating the opera -
tion of the three energy flows, and the efficient utilization of energy can 
be guaranteed. Moreover, the system is attached to the main grid (MG), 
which can improve the economy and flexibility of system operation 
through interaction with the MG. Fig. 1 shows the configuration and the 
energy flows of the RES-CCHP system. 
Particularly, the electrical energy flow comprises four components: 
MG, power generation units (PGU), wind turbines (WT), and electricity 
storage units (ESU). The cooling energy flow comprises an electric 
chiller (EC) and an absorption chiller (AC). The heat energy flow pri -
marily comprises the gas boiler (GB), heat recovery devices (HRD), heat 
exchanger (HE), and heat storage units (HSU). The primary functions of 
these components are listed as follows: (1) PGU and GB consume natural 
gas to generate electricity and heat, respectively. (2) EC and AC convert 
electricity and heat energy into cooling energy, respectively. (3) The 
waste heat of the PGU, including flue gas waste heat and jacket water 
heat, can be recovered through HR. (4) The heat energy is converted by 
HE to meet the heating demand. (5) The energy storage units (ESU and 
HSU) can provide more operational flexibility for system operation.

3. Uncertainty ROF and RMPC-based OS 
3.1. Integrated uncertainty ROF 
Herein, an integrated uncertainty ROF was established to explore the 
collaboration between PMs and uncertain OSs in the optimal scheduling 
of RES-CCHP systems. The integrated optimization framework com -
prises three parts ( Fig. 2 ): (1) predicted probability distribution, (2) 
uncertainty rolling optimization, and (3) historical data update. 
Under this framework, first, a prediction model of the probability 
distribution was constructed to predict the source-load and its corre -
sponding error interval. Because the electrical load changes quickly and 
the cooling and heating loads change slowly, different time scales were 
used for the part of the predicted probability distribution. Then, the 
obtained forecast data was input into the part of uncertain rolling 
optimization, and the uncertain rolling OS was applied to optimize the 
economic dispatch in multiple uncertain environments. Moreover, the 
part of the historical data update could use the latest source-load data 
under the ROF to improve the prediction accuracy of the probability 
distribution by updating the historical data. 
The prediction of electrical, cooling, and heating energies on 
different time scales is shown in Fig. 3 . The prediction time interval of 
electrical energy (including RES generation and electrical load) is set as 
Δ s , and the prediction time interval of cooling and heating energy is set 
as Δ l . At time t , based on historical data, the probability distribution of 
electrical cooling and heating energies is predicted simultaneously. At 
time t + Δ s , only the probability distribution of electric energy is pre -
dicted, and at time t + Δ l , the probability distribution of electrical 
cooling and heating energies is predicted simultaneously. Similarly, in 
the part of historical data update, the time resolution of the electrical 
energy update historical data is Δ s , and the resolution of the cooling and 
heating energy update historical data is Δ l . 
3.2. RMPC-based OS 
Based on the integrated uncertainty ROF, an RMPC-based OS was 
proposed. The OS comprises two parts. During optimization, the prob -
ability distribution of the source-load prediction was determined first. 
Afterward, the equipment scheduling was optimized through a robust 
OS according to the probability distribution information to meet the 
supply and demand requirements. At the next time interval, the pre -
dicted probability distribution and robust optimization were recon -
ducted based on the latest source-load information. The flowchart of the 
proposed OS is shown in Fig. 4 .  
1) GPR-based source-load prediction: Predictions were performed with 
different time scales for RES and the load. In the prediction time 
horizon, the source-load probability distribution (predicted value 
and its corresponding error) can be realized by the GPR method 
according to the historical data.  
2) Min-max rolling optimization: Min-max rolling optimization was 
performed within each time interval using the probability distribu -
tion information to minimize the operating costs under an uncertain 
scenario over the given optimization time horizon. 
The flow of the proposed OS is summarized as follows: 
Step 1: Set the prediction and rolling optimization time horizons. 
Step 2: For each time interval, update the source-load data according 
to the latest state of the system and obtain the probability distribution of 
RES and the load forecast through the GPR-based source-load 
prediction. 
Step 3: Obtain the source-load predicted value and corresponding 
error through the probability distribution. 
Step 4: Perform the min – max rolling optimization with the predic -
tion information from Step 3 and implement the optimization

5.3. Comparison with traditional MPC OS 
To verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed OS, the 
RMPC-based OS was compared to a traditional MPC-based (TMPC- 
based) OS. The TMPC-based OS does not consider the existence of the 
prediction error, thereby outperforming the RMPC-based OS in terms of 
operating economy. However, it lacks robustness in system operation. 
With uncertain source-loads, the scheduling strategy, determined based 
on TMPC, deviates from the actual load, and these imbalances must be 
compensated by the MG, which increases the TMPC-based OS cost.

5.4. Comparison with day-ahead robust OS 
The day-ahead robust OS formulates the scheduling strategy for the 
whole day of the next day in an uncertain scenario, and the source-load 
information of the second day cannot be applied. In the RMPC-based 
optimization, prediction and optimization are implemented under the 
uncertainty ROF. The source-load information of the next day can be 
applied to reduce forecast deviation and system operating costs. In the 
day-ahead robust optimization, the maximum error obtained by the 
GPR-based PM is selected as its uncertainty scenario to cope with the 
source-load uncertainty of the next day. To better prove the advantages

6. Conclusion 
Because of the multiple uncertainties of RES-CCHP systems, an in -
tegrated uncertainty ROF is established and an OS based on an RMPC is 
proposed. Case studies are used to verify the effectiveness and superi -
ority of the proposed framework and OS. The following conclusions can 
be summarized:  
(1). In the source-load uncertainty scenario, the TMPC-based OS does 
not consider the source-load uncertainty, and the resulting 
compensation cost increases the total operating cost. The RMPC- 
based OS can obtain a robust system scheduling plan, reducing 
the operating cost by 11.5% compared with the TMPC-based OS.
